# FastAPI rules

Apply these rules to every FastAPI endpoint, Pydantic model and API test you write or review. The first section is always in force; open a rule from the table when the task touches it.

## Always apply (critical, high)

### Give every endpoint a response model and list its real error statuses in responses

_high · python, fastapi_

**Rule.** Declare `response_model` (or a return annotation) on every endpoint and list every error status it can return in `responses`, with the error model.

**Why.** Without a response model nothing filters the output, so an ORM object leaks columns such as password hashes, and undeclared errors are missing from the spec, so generated clients cannot handle them.

**Correct:**

```python
@router.get(
    "/{user_id}",
    response_model=UserOut,
    responses={404: {"model": ProblemDetail}},
)
async def get_user(user_id: int) -> UserOut: ...
```

### Generate the OpenAPI document from the FastAPI app and never edit it by hand

_high · python, fastapi_

**Rule.** Treat the FastAPI app and its Pydantic models as the only source of the OpenAPI document. Export it in CI with `app.openapi()` and never edit the exported file.

**Why.** A hand-edited spec drifts from the code, so clients and docs generated from it call endpoints that no longer behave that way.

**Correct:**

```bash
python -c "import json; from myapp.main import app; print(json.dumps(app.openapi()))" > openapi.json
```

| Impact | Rule | Applies to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| medium | [Compare the spec with the main branch using oasdiff and fail on breaking changes](references/rules.md#compare-the-spec-with-the-main-branch-using-oasdiff-and-fail-on-breaking-changes) — oasdiff breaking reports removed fields and tightened types between two spec versions. | python, oasdiff |
| medium | [Turn off the built-in docs and openapi.json endpoints on a public API](references/rules.md#turn-off-the-built-in-docs-and-openapijson-endpoints-on-a-public-api) — A public API publishes a static reference; /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json stay only behind network authentication. | python, fastapi |
| medium | [Mark an endpoint deprecated and send Deprecation and Sunset headers before removing it](references/rules.md#mark-an-endpoint-deprecated-and-send-deprecation-and-sunset-headers-before-removing-it) — deprecated=True shows in the spec; the headers tell machine clients when it goes away. | python, fastapi |
| medium | [Replace dependencies with app.dependency_overrides in API tests](references/rules.md#replace-dependencies-with-appdependency_overrides-in-api-tests) — Overrides swap the injected dependency for the test; patching import paths ties the test to module layout. | python, fastapi, pytest |
| medium | [Return every API error in one Problem Details model](references/rules.md#return-every-api-error-in-one-problem-details-model) — One RFC 9457 shape (type, title, status, detail) for all endpoints, declared in responses. | python, fastapi |
| medium | [Set operation_id explicitly so generated SDK method names stay stable](references/rules.md#set-operation_id-explicitly-so-generated-sdk-method-names-stay-stable) — The default id is built from the function and path, so a rename changes every client method name. | python, fastapi |
| medium | [Run Schemathesis against the OpenAPI document and fix the code, not the test](references/rules.md#run-schemathesis-against-the-openapi-document-and-fix-the-code-not-the-test) — It generates requests from the spec and finds 5xx errors, schema mismatches and undeclared statuses. | python, schemathesis |
| low | [Describe every field and parameter of a public model and add an example](references/rules.md#describe-every-field-and-parameter-of-a-public-model-and-add-an-example) — Field(description=..., examples=[...]) and Path/Query(description=...) reach the spec and the generated docs. | python, fastapi |
| low | [Lint the OpenAPI document with Spectral in CI and fail on warnings](references/rules.md#lint-the-openapi-document-with-spectral-in-ci-and-fail-on-warnings) — Spectral checks one spec against the spectral:oas ruleset plus team rules for naming and descriptions. | python, spectral |
